tests.name: TestScenarios/001-read-env-denied
tests.why: A credential-shaped file inside the repository: the path denylist wins before the read happens, so the canary never enters the log.

tests.name: TestScenarios/002-read-outside-repo
tests.why: The repo pin: nothing above the repository root is readable.

tests.name: TestScenarios/003-key-file-in-subdir
tests.why: Denylist globs apply at any depth.

tests.name: TestScenarios/004-curl-needs-confirm
tests.why: A network tool on the command line is the bootstrap stand-in for the egress check: it cannot run without the user. The confirm is an ordinary one (not a security confirm), so a standing approval the person gave for curl may answer it.

tests.name: TestScenarios/005-read-readme-allowed
tests.why: A plain file inside the repository reads silently.

tests.name: TestScenarios/006-write-in-the-folder
tests.why: A write inside the repository goes ahead without asking (ADR 35, approval.writes = "allow", the default): its diff is logged and its previous content kept. What follows is what still asks or refuses.

tests.name: TestScenarios/007-env-through-shell
tests.why: shell-exec cannot run without the user, by an ordinary confirm a standing approval for sh may answer; and even when it does, the child environment is scrubbed (see internal/prim tests).

tests.name: TestScenarios/008-symlink-escape
tests.why: escape-link is a symlink inside the repo pointing at ../outside.txt. The pin resolves links before judging, so the link does not escape.

tests.name: TestScenarios/009-literal-key-on-argv
tests.why: L1 (P4): a known-shape key on a command line is denied outright, before the network-tool confirm even gets a say.

tests.name: TestScenarios/010-file-content-to-unbound-host
tests.why: L2 (P6), the spec's own example: file content piped into an egress body. The scenario runner's guard has no binding table, so collect.example is a destination nothing authorises, and the provenance tag on the string is what names the source in the denial.

tests.name: TestScenarios/011-wipe-is-not-the-models
tests.why: L2 (P6): the model may not strip provenance. The escape hatch belongs to the user (SPEC Risk 1); scenarios run with model origin.

tests.name: TestScenarios/012-command-from-file-content
tests.why: L2 (P6): a command line assembled from tool output is the classic indirect-injection path, so it is a security confirm naming the source. The runner answers no.

tests.name: TestScenarios/013-write-to-a-hook-asks
tests.why: A protected path holds code that later runs with the user's authority (a git hook here): a write there is a security confirm, which no standing approval waives, writes in the folder included.

tests.name: TestScenarios/014-credential-in-a-write-asks
tests.why: L1 (P4): content that looks like a credential is a security confirm, even where writes go ahead without asking.

tests.name: TestScenarios/015-write-through-a-link-denied
tests.why: Writes in the folder go ahead, but only in the folder: escape-link points at ../outside.txt, and the pin resolves links before judging.

tests.name: TestScenarios/016-credential-in-an-edit-asks
tests.why: L1 (P4): an edit's replacement is written content, so a credential in it is a security confirm, as in a whole-file write (014).

tests.name: TestScenarios/017-credential-in-a-later-edit-asks
tests.why: A call with several edits (ADR 38) is judged as a single edit is: each edit's new is written content, so a credential in the second one is the same security confirm as in 016, though the first edit is harmless.

tests.name: TestScenarios/018-edit-through-a-placeholder-does-not-open-a-denied-file
tests.why: ADR 43: fs-edit matches old in the text the model reads, with each credential a placeholder. That is no way into a credential file: the path is refused before the file is read, whatever old says.

tests.name: TestScenarios/019-key-then-private-key-in-a-write-asks
tests.why: Redaction (P7): a key written ahead of a private key came out of the L1 scan after it, and the log writer's redaction pass sliced backwards over it and panicked. The write is still a security confirm, and neither credential reaches the log.

tests.name: TestScenarios/020-key-typed-into-a-page
tests.why: L1 (P4), ADR 62: what is typed into a page in the task's browser is an egress payload, since the page can send it on to its site. A known-shape key in it is refused outright, before the confirm every action on a page asks: no binding names the listed site (shop.example) for its class, and the browser, like a contained MCP server, is judged by every site it can reach. The browser never starts.

tests.name: TestScenarios/021-click-in-the-browser-asks
tests.why: ADR 62: a click in the task's browser can pay, delete or send what was typed, so every action on a page asks, as an MCP tool that acts does. It is an ordinary confirm, which [approval] commands may give to the judge; reading a page asks nothing. Answered no, the browser never starts.
